title: Antares in the Wild: Testing on Two New Cybersecurity Benchmarks
date_source: Dateline printed on the post itself: 'July 28, 2026' (cisco-foundation-ai.github.io blog page, re-verified HTTP 200 on 2026-08-31).
rule_cited: §1 (Cisco/Robust Intelligence is a registered third-party evaluator and measured the named frontier-developer models itself in its own harness; the surviving row's subjects are not Cisco's own models), §2 (measured results, same harness, each model run 3x), §4 (Tier B: Gate 1 yes, Gate 2 limb (c) fails - comparative ranking / cost-efficiency study, no dangerous threshold crossed), §5 (comparators/baselines are never rows -> Notes [Report tested: ...]), FRONTIER-MODEL RULE.
screening_ledger: Former finding [1] (Antares-350M / 1B / 3B self-reported recall and the Devin-rebuild comparison) removed from the dataset and logged as 'EXCLUDED - company self-report' under §1 (Cisco reporting on its own Antares models with no external evaluator named; CyberGym and Matt Rickard are benchmark authors, not contributing evaluators). Secondary grounds: FRONTIER-MODEL RULE (350M-3B task-specific vulnerability-localization models are non-frontier) and §2/§2.1 (Antares Devin-rebuild figures self-labelled 'Estimated - extrapolated from Matt Rickard's public 34/50 rebuild'; Devin/Claude/Codex baselines lifted from Cognition's July 2026 post).

findings.finding: Cisco Foundation AI ran 15 models through its own CyberGym-localization harness (each model run 3x, mean reported) on ~1,500 real OSS-Fuzz vulnerabilities and found GPT-5.5 localised the vulnerable file in 89.1% of tasks at $333 per run, ahead of GPT-5-mini (85.9%, $46), GPT-OSS-120B (69.5%, $58), GPT-4o (57.9%, $32) and GPT-5-nano (54.5%, $9).
findings.finding_quote: Recall = share of tasks where the model found at least one of the patched files. Same harness for every model.
findings.notes: [Report tested: Kimi-K3, GLM-5.2, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-2B, Antares-3B, Antares-1B, Antares-350M]
findings.tier_reasoning: Gate 1 yes - Cisco's own measured recall figures for named released frontier-developer models on a public cyber benchmark. Gate 2 limb (c) fails: an explicit comparative ranking plus cost-efficiency ('Intelligence Density') study with no dangerous threshold crossed, in which the hosted models are instruments for positioning Cisco's own Antares family, so no company response is reasonably expected. eval=yes / action=no. §4b does not exclude: vulnerability-localization recall is a cyber-capability measurement, not a generic factuality/correctness benchmark. Quote is the chart caption (character-exact) because the numbers appear only as chart/table labels and no prose sentence states them.
